 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE  FIR/ORDER) NO. 18944 of 2014  ==========================================================
 DIPAKBHAI JEKISHANBHAI RANA  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ORS.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR ADIL R MIRZA(2488) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR SATYAM Y CHHAYA(3242) for the Respondent(s) No. 2  NOTICE SERVED BY DS for the Respondent(s) No. 3  MR. CHINTAN DAVE, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 08/10/2025

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

Heard learned Senior Advocate Mr. R.R. Marshal, assisted by learned Advocate Mr. Adil R. Mirza for the petitioner; learned Advocate Mr. Satyam Chhaya for the private respondent; and learned APP for the respondent-State.

2. Learned Senior Advocate Mr. R.R. Marshal has submitted that a plain reading of the FIR, in its entirety, would reveal that, at the highest, the allegations therein may constitute a complaint falling within the ambit of Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, inasmuch as the cheque issued by the petitioner is alleged to have been returned unpaid.
It is urged that the ingredients necessary to constitute the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code are conspicuously absent.

sentences.text:
It is further contended that even upon a holistic reading of the FIR, it unmistakably emanates that the transaction in question is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18944/2014 ORDER DATED:
08/10/2025 undefined purely of a monetary or commercial nature, which has been ingeniously clothed with the trappings of criminality.

Such an attempt, it is submitted, has been consistently deprecated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a catena of authoritative pronouncements holding that a mere breach of contractual or financial obligation, sans dishonest or fraudulent intent at inception, does not attract the rigours of penal law.
2.3. In view of the foregoing submissions, it is fervently urged that the present petition deserves to be allowed and the impugned proceedings quashed in the interest of justice.

3. Per contra, learned advocate for the private respondent submitted that the cheque in question had been handed over to the complainant with an assurance that the same would be duly encashed;
however, it was subsequently dishonoured as the petitioner had issued specific instructions to the bank to stop its payment.
It is, therefore, contended that such conduct, prima facie, attracts the ingredients of the offence of cheating as defined under Section 415 of the Indian Penal Code.
3.1. In view of the foregoing, it is earnestly prayed that the present petition be dismissed.
4. Learned APP for the respondent-State, while adopting the submissions advanced by the learned advocate for the private respondent, has also urged that the petition be dismissed.

5. Upon a perusal of the FIR, it transpires that the gravamen of the allegations pertains to a monetary transaction of 5,00,000/-
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18944/2014 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined between the petitioner and the complainant, wherein the cheque issued by the petitioner was returned unpaid on account of "stop payment" instructions.

Consequently, the complainant approached the Valsad City Police Station, Valsad, and lodged the FIR invoking Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code,
alleging criminal breach of trust and cheating against the petitioner.

5.1. This Court, upon a plain and meaningful reading of the FIR, fails to comprehend as to how the mere act of stopping the payment of a cheque could, by any stretch of legal imagination, attract the ingredients of the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
At the highest, such conduct may, if the statutory preconditions are satisfied, give rise to an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
The present prosecution, therefore, appears to be a manifest attempt to impart a criminal colour to a transaction that is, in its essence, civil in nature.
Such misuse of the criminal process deserves to be deprecated and ought to be nipped in the bud.

5.2. In the case of Vesa Holdings Pvt. Ltd. and another vs. State of Kerala and others - (2015) 8 SCC 293], Hon'ble Apex Court made the following observation:-

sentences.text: It is true that a given set of facts may make out a civil wrong as also a criminal offence and only because a civil remedy may be available to the complainant that itself cannot be ground to quash a criminal proceeding.
The real test is whether the allegations in the complaint disclose the criminal offence of cheating or not.
In the present case, there is nothing to show that at the very inception there was any inception on behalf of an accused person to cheat which is a condition precedent for an offence u/s 420 IPC.
In our view, the complaint does not disclose any criminal NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18944/2014 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2025 undefined offence at all.
Criminal proceedings should not be encouraged when it is found to be mala fide or otherwise an abuse of the process of the courts.
Superior courts while exercising this power should also strive to serve the ends of justice.

In our opinion, in view of these facts allowing the police investigation to continue would amount to an abuse of the process of the court and the High Court committed an error in refusing to exercise the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C to quash the proceedings."
5.3. In view of the above, continuation of the criminal proceedings would be an abuse of process of law.
6. Accordingly, the present petition deserves to be and is hereby ALLOWED.

The complaint being C.R. No. I-215 of 2014 registered with Valsad City Police Station, along with all consequential proceedings arising therefrom, is hereby quashed and set aside qua the petitioner herein.

(J. C. DOSHI,J) MANISH MISHRA Dipakbhai Jekishanbhai Rana vs State Of Gujarat on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98742672/
